targets.title: Face of a fighter: Bizygomatic width as a cue of formidability.
targets.evidence_quote: In the present work, we conducted three studies that aimed to directly replicate and extend the findings of Zilioli et al. ( 2014 ).
targets.outcome_quote: In the present work, we successfully replicated their main finding that the manual fWHRbrow measurement predicted men's fighting success (Study 2). We then successfully extended their work, finding associations between fWHR and grappling abilities, as a metric of aggression (Studies 1–3). This association between fWHR and overall fighting success only held when we used Zilioli et al.'s ( 2014 ) original methodology (overall fighter data) and did not conceptually replicate when using fight‐specific data.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The manual direct replication worked, whereas the automatic replication and the explicitly labelled conceptual replication did not. The discussion explicitly contrasts successful original-methodology and unsuccessful conceptual attempts. Conclusion sentences confirming the association do not resolve these conflicting attempts as a whole; the codebook specifically classifies a working close replication alongside a failed conceptual replication as mixed.
